arxiv-2101-08528.title: Electric dipole polarizability in neutron-rich Sn isotopes as a probe of nuclear isovector properties
arxiv-2101-08528.creator: Z. Z. Li, Y. F. Niu, W. H. Long
arxiv-2101-08528.description: Abstract The determination of nuclear symmetry energy, and in particular, its density dependence, is a long-standing problem for nuclear physics community. Previous studies have found that the product of electric dipole polarizability α D \alpha_{D} and symmetry energy at saturation density J J has a strong linear correlation with L L , the slope parameter of symmetry energy.

arxiv-2104-10968.title: Barriers and Opportunities to Accessible Social Media Content Authoring
arxiv-2104-10968.creator: Letícia Seixas Pereira, José Coelho, André Rodrigues
arxiv-2104-10968.description: Abstract User-generated content plays a key role in social networking, allowing a more active participation, socialisation, and collaboration among users. In particular, media content has been gaining a lot of ground, allowing users to express themselves through different types of formats such as images, GIFs and videos.

arxiv-2105-07525.creator: Tuomas Hakoniemi
arxiv-2105-07525.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Tuomas Hakoniemi. arxiv-2110-15274.title: Degenerate Local-dimension-invariant Stabilizer Codes and an Alternative Bound for the Distance Preservation Condition
arxiv-2110-15274.creator: Lane G. Gunderman
arxiv-2110-15274.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Lane G. Gunderman. One hurdle to performing reliable quantum computations is overcoming noise. One possibility is to reduce the number of particles needing to be protected from noise and instead use systems with more states, so called qudit quantum computers.

arxiv-2207-06736.title: On the numerical solution of Volterra integral equations on equispaced nodes Thanks: The authors are member of the INdAM Research group GNCS and the TAA-UMI Research Group. This research has been accomplished within “Research ITalian network on Approximation” (RITA).
arxiv-2207-06736.creator: Luisa Fermo, Domenico Mezzanotte, Donatella Occorsio
arxiv-2207-06736.description: Abstract In the present paper, a Nyström-type method for second kind Volterra integral equations is introduced and studied. The method makes use of generalized Bernstein polynomials, defined for continuous functions and based on equally spaced points. Stability and convergence are studied in the space of continuous functions, and some numerical tests illustrate the performance of the proposed approach.

arxiv-2211-13740.title: Cutting Medusa’s Path Tackling Kill-Chains with Quantum Computing
arxiv-2211-13740.creator: Mark Carney
arxiv-2211-13740.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mark Carney. This paper embarks upon exploration of quantum vulnerability analysis. By introducing vulnerability graphs, related to attack graphs, this paper provides background theory and a subsequent method for solving significant cybersecurity problems with quantum computing. The example given is to prioritize patches by expressing the connectivity of various vulnerabilities on a network with a QUBO and then solving this with quantum annealing. Such a solution is then proved to remove all kill-chains (paths to security compromise) on a network.

arxiv-2306-00226.title: Human-centric Literature on Trust for SfTI Veracity Spearhead
arxiv-2306-00226.creator: Kelly Blincoe, Markus Luczak-Roesch, Tim Miller, Matthias Galster
arxiv-2306-00226.description: Abstract This article summarizes the literature on trust of digital technologies from a human-centric perspective. We summarize literature on trust in face-to-face interactions from other fields, followed by a discussion of organizational trust, technology-mediated trust, trust of software products, trust of AI, and blockchain.

arxiv-2402-04063.title: Evidence of temperature-dependent interplay between spin and orbital moment in van der Waals ferromagnet VI 3
arxiv-2402-04063.creator: A. De Vita, R. Sant, V. Polewczyk, G. van der Laan, N. B. Brookes, T. Kong, R. J. Cava, G. Rossi, G. Vinai, G. Panaccione

Van der Waals materials provide a versatile toolbox for the emergence of new quantum phenomena and the fabrication of functional heterostructures. Among them, the trihalide VI 3 stands out for its unique magnetic and structural landscape.

arxiv-2402-17180.title: Performance analysis of MUSIC-type imaging without diagonal elements of multi-static response matrix
arxiv-2402-17180.creator: Won-Kwang Park
arxiv-2402-17180.description: Abstract Generally, to apply the MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm for the rapid imaging of small inhomogeneities, the complete elements of the multi-static response (MSR) matrix must be collected. However, in real-world applications such as microwave imaging or bistatic measurement configuration, diagonal elements of the MSR matrix are unknown.

arxiv-2407-08695.title: Lower T-count with faster algorithms
arxiv-2407-08695.creator: Vivien Vandaele
arxiv-2407-08695.description: Abstract Among the cost metrics characterizing a quantum circuit, the T T -count stands out as one of the most crucial as its minimization is particularly important in various areas of quantum computation such as fault-tolerant quantum computing and quantum circuit simulation.

arxiv-2502-11697.title: MVTokenFlow: High-quality 4D Content Generation using Multiview Token Flow
arxiv-2502-11697.creator: Hanzhuo Huang, Yuan Liu, Ge Zheng, Jiepeng Wang, Zhiyang Dou, Sibei Yang
arxiv-2502-11697.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hanzhuo Huang, Yuan Liu, Ge Zheng, Jiepeng Wang, Zhiyang Dou, Sibei Yang. In this paper, we present MVTokenFlow for high-quality 4D content creation from monocular videos. Recent advancements in generative models such as video diffusion models and multiview diffusion models enable us to create videos or 3D models. However, extending these generative models for dynamic 4D content creation is still a challenging task that requires the generated content to be consistent spatially and temporally.

arxiv-2503-10181.title: Bayesian analysis of a (3+1)D hybrid approach with initial conditions from hadronic transport
arxiv-2503-10181.creator: Niklas Götz 1,2 , Iurii Karpenko 3 and Hannah Elfner 4,1,2,5
arxiv-2503-10181.description: Abstract Background The SMASH-vHLLE-hybrid model integrates the SMASH transport code for the hadronic phase and the vHLLE hydrodynamic model for the QGP phase in heavy-ion collisions. Bayesian analysis offers a robust statistical method to constrain model parameters of a hybrid approach and evaluate uncertainties by comparing predictions with experimental data.

arxiv-2509-14280.title: Solving Fermat-type equations over quadratic fields
arxiv-2509-14280.creator: Begum Gulsah Cakti
arxiv-2509-14280.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Begum Gulsah Cakti. This paper applies the modular approach to obtain effectively computable bounds for Fermat-type equations over number fields, while also discussing the differences and obstructions that arise when considering such equations over totally real versus totally complex number fields. We use these techniques to study the generalized Fermat equation d r ​ a p + b p + c p = 0 d^{r}a^{p}+b^{p}+c^{p}=0 over quadratic fields ℚ ⁡ ( d ) {\mathbb{Q}}(\sqrt{d}) of class number one.

arxiv-2601-03180.title: Strongly finitary metric monads are too strong
arxiv-2601-03180.creator: Jiří Adámek
arxiv-2601-03180.description: Abstract . Varieties of quantitative algebras are fully described by their free-algebra monads on the category 𝐌𝐞𝐭 \operatorname{\bf Met} of metric spaces. For a longer time it has been an open problem whether the resulting enriched monads are precisely the strongly finitary ones (determined by their values on finite discrete spaces).

pmc-11432946.title: Replicative Endothelial Cell Senescence May Lead to Endothelial Dysfunction by Increasing the BH2/BH4 Ratio Induced by Oxidative Stress, Reducing BH4 Availability, and Decreasing the Expression of eNOS
pmc-11432946.creator: Ignacio Hernandez-Navarro, Laura Botana, Javier Diez-Mata, Laura Tesoro, Beatriz Jimenez-Guirado, Claudia Gonzalez-Cucharero, Nunzio Alcharani, Jose Luis Zamorano, Marta Saura, Carlos Zaragoza, Jeffrey L Platt
pmc-11432946.description: Vascular aging is associated with the development of cardiovascular complications, in which endothelial cell senescence (ES) may play a critical role. Nitric oxide (NO) prevents human ES through inhibition of oxidative stress, and inflammatory signaling by mechanisms yet to be elucidated.

pmc-11453222.title: 12606 Gamification In The Management Of Children And Adolescents With Diabetes: A Systematic Review
pmc-11453222.creator: Larissa C Hespanhol, Vanessa Lins de Menezes, Paula Christianne G G Souto Maia, Caroline Cristine Almeida Balieiro, Wellgner Fernandes Oliveira Amador, Rafaelle C Lira
pmc-11453222.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Lins de Menezes: None. Oliveira Amador: None. Background: Educating children and adolescents with diabetes about their own condition presents a significant challenge. Gamification has been proposed as an innovative approach to ease the transition to self-care by engaging and empowering children and adolescents in their diabetes management. Purpose: The purpose of this systematic review is to examine published research on using gamification and technology within diabetes care for young patients.

pmc-11469955.title: Oral syphilis - the great imitator: a series of six cases
pmc-11469955.creator: Brian Maloney, Claire M Healy
pmc-11469955.description: Syphilis is an infectious disease which can present with multitudinous mucocutaneous manifestations. Often referred to as the ‘great mimicker', syphilis can present with non-specific symptoms and has a tropism for various organ systems. The oral cavity has been identified as a site commonly affected in the early stages of syphilis infection.

pmc-12386288.title: Construction and Analysis of Immune Infiltration and Competing Endogenous RNA Network in Moyamoya Disease
pmc-12386288.creator: Wenhao Liu, Hanhui Fu, Shiyuan Fang, Jun Ni, Bin Peng
pmc-12386288.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a cerebrovascular condition characterized by progressive stenosis of intracranial arteries, leading to stroke. While MMD was long considered a genetic disorder, emerging evidence suggests autoimmune mechanisms may contribute to its pathogenesis. The role of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) in the pathogenesis of MMD is under heated discussion, and a competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network involving MMD-related ncRNAs has not been constructed.

pmc-12487686.title: A systematic process to formulate quality lessons learned about hospital resilience during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-12487686.creator: Roula Haddad, Christian Dagenais, Muriel Kielende, Aurélie Hot, Valéry Ridde
pmc-12487686.description: BackgroundThe urgency of the COVID-19 pandemic forced hospitals to adjust swiftly to the health crisis. They adopted a variety of solutions and encountered numerous challenges. To enhance hospitals’ readiness for future crises, the HoSPiCOVID research project documented the experiences of seven hospitals in five countries (Brazil, Canada, France, Japan, Mali) to extract quality lessons learned (QLLs).

pmc-13316561.title: Development and Clinical Validation of a Protocol-Agnostic Machine Learning Platform for Automated Treatment Planning in External Beam Radiation Therapy
pmc-13316561.creator: Julie K. Shade, Pranav Lakshminarayanan, Peter Hoban, Michael Bowers, Kevin Gorman, Saida Muktar Reshid, Thomas Lilieholm, Christian Velten, Siddharth Kapoor, Tyler Smith, David Murray, Wolfgang A. Tomé, Harry Quon, Daniel Y. Song, Todd McNutt
pmc-13316561.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeTo develop and validate a protocol-agnostic machine learning platform (“Predictive Planning”) for knowledge-based planning (KBP) in external beam radiation therapy.Methods and MaterialsFive thousand three hundred thirty-four retrospective photon beam treatment plans (1145 Head and Neck [H&N], 1623 Thoracic, 781 Abdominal, 1785 Pelvis) from 2 institutions were used to develop and internally test general-purpose models for organ at risk (OAR) dose-volume histogram prediction.
